body_md:
\label{rmk:mu-large}
We note that condition \eqref{ass:Loj-L2} implies that  for $\varepsilon>0$ chosen sufficiently small the factor $\mu$ is guaranteed to be larger than any fixed constant, as desired in our analysis of maps that are close to simple bubble trees. We also note that the claimed estimate is trivially true for maps whose tension is bounded away from zero and that the claim is invariant under translation. In the following, we can hence restrict our attention to maps with
$\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}\leq \delta_1$
which are constant outside of $\mathbb{D}_3$ and satisfy \eqref{ass:Loj-L2} for $a=0$ and $\mu\geq \mu_0$, where $\delta_1>0$ and $\mu_0 >1$ are sufficiently small/large constants that are chosen below and that only depend on $N$ and $\omega^*$.

label: est:Loj-dual
title: Proof
body_md:
As the $L^\infty$ and $\dot H^1$ norms are conformally invariant the assumption \eqref{ass:Loj-L2} ensures that  
$ \widetilde u:=u\circ \pi_{a,\mu}^{-1}:S^2\to N$
satisfies the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{prop:Loj-Simon}. We hence deduce that 
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned} \label{est:Loj-dual}
\vertE(u)-E(\omega^*)\vert
&=
\vertE(\widetilde u)-E(\omega^*)\vert
\leq
C \VertdE(\widetilde u)\Vert_{H^{-1}(S^2, g_{S^2})}^\gamma
=
C \VertdE(u)\Vert_{*,(a,\mu)}^\gamma,
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
where $\Vert\cdot\Vert_{*,(a,\mu)}$ denotes the dual norm to the weighted
$H^1$ norm
\begin{equation} \label{def:weighted-H1}
\Vertv\Vert_{(a,\mu)}
:=
\Vertv\Vert_{H^1(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2,g_{a,\mu})} \text{ for }
g_{a,\mu}
=
\pi_{a,\mu}^*g_{S^2}.
\end{equation}

We note that
\begin{equation*}
\Vertv\Vert_{L^2(\mathbb{D}_2)}
\leq C
(\log\mu)^\frac{1}{2} \cdot \Vertv\Vert_{(a,\mu)},
\end{equation*}
compare e.g. (2.27) of \cite{rupflinharmonic} and hence that
\begin{equation*}
C\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\mathbb{D}_2)}
\geq
(\log\mu)^{-1/2}\VertdE(u)\Vert_{*,(a,\mu)}. 
\end{equation*}
The estimate \eqref{est:Loj-dual} hence allows us to deduce that 
\begin{equation} \label{est:Loj-with-logmu}
\vertE(u)-E(\omega^*)\vert
\leq
C(\log\mu)^{\gamma/2}
\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^\gamma
\end{equation}
holds 
for any $u$ for which the assumptions of  Proposition~\ref{prop:Loj-L^2} are satisfied for $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_1$.

For maps $u$ for which $\log \mu$ is bounded by some fixed multiple of $\vert\log(\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)})\vert$, so in particular whenever
$
\mu
\leq
\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^{-8}
$, 
we hence immediately get the estimate \eqref{claim:Loj-L2} claimed
in Proposition~\ref{prop:Loj-L^2}.

It thus remains to consider the case where 
$\mu
\geq
\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^{-8}$. In this case
 we should expect to obtain stronger estimates since the
$L^2$ norm of the tension strongly weighs the
highly concentrated region while the contribution of the bulk should be controlled quadratically in
terms of the tension since constant maps are
non-degenerate critical points of the energy.
Indeed, we can show


\textbf{Claim:}
There exists $\varepsilon\in (0,\varepsilon_1]$ and $C$ so that 
the  estimate 
\begin{equation*}
\vertE(u)-E(\omega^*)\vert
\leq
C\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^2
\end{equation*} 
holds for any map $u$ which satisfies the assumptions
of Proposition~\ref{prop:Loj-L^2} for some 
\begin{equation}\label{ass:case2}
\mu \geq \Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^{-8}.
\end{equation}

For the proof of this claim we can use 
standard results on the energy
on neck regions of almost harmonic maps, as found e.g. in Lemma~2.9 of \cite{toppingannals}. These imply that there exist constants $\delta_{1,2}>0$ and $K$ depending only on $N$ so that for maps $v:\mathbb{D}_1\to N$ with $\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\mathbb{D}_1)}\leq\delta_1 $ 
the estimate 
\begin{equation}
E\bigl(v,\mathbb{D}_{e r}\setminus \mathbb{D}_{r}\bigr)
\leq
K r
\label{est:neck-Peter}
\end{equation} 
holds for all $r\in(0,e^{-1})$ for which  
\begin{equation}\label{ass:E-small-neck}
E\bigl(v,\mathbb{D}_1\setminus \mathbb{D}_{r^2}\bigr)<\delta_2. 
\end{equation}



\begin{proof}[Proof of claim]
As discussed above we can assume that $a=0$ and that $\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}\leq \delta_1$  where $\delta_1=\delta_1(N)>0$ is as above. For $\varepsilon$ sufficiently small we immediately get from 
\eqref{ass:Loj-L2} that the 
smallness of the energy required in \eqref{ass:E-small-neck} holds for any radius $r\geq \Lambda \mu^{-1/2}$, $\Lambda$ a sufficiently large constant that only depends only on $N$ and $\omega^*$. 
We can hence obtain a radius $r_1\sim \mu^{-1/2}$ for which
\begin{equation} \label{est:energy-A-larger}
E\bigl(u,\mathbb{D}_{8r_1}\setminus \mathbb{D}_{r_1/8}\bigr)
\lesssim
\mu^{-1/2},
\end{equation}
where here and in the following we write $\lesssim$  if the corresponding inequality holds up to a multiplicative constant $C$ that only depends on $\omega^*$ and $N$ and use $\sim $ if both $\lesssim $ and $\gtrsim $ hold.  

Setting
$
A:=\mathbb{D}_{2r_1}\setminus \mathbb{D}_{r_1/2}
$ and $ m:=\fint_A u
$ we can now use that 
\begin{equation*}
\Vertu-m\Vert_{L^\infty(A)}\leq \text{osc}_A u
\leq
\text{osc}_A(\omega^*\circ\pi_\mu)
+
2\Vertu-\omega^*\circ\pi_\mu\Vert_{L^\infty}
\lesssim
(r_1\mu)^{-1/2}+\varepsilon\leq \mu^{-1/2}+\varepsilon
\end{equation*}
can be made smaller than any given positive constant by choosing $\varepsilon$ sufficiently small, compare Remark \ref{rmk:mu-large}. In particular, $m$ will be contained in a small tubular neighbourhood of $N$ on which the nearest point projection $\pi_N$ is well defined and smooth.
Fixing cut-off functions 
$\varphi_{1,2}$ with  
\begin{equation*}
\varphi_1\equiv1 \text{ on }\mathbb{D}_{r_1}
\text{ and }
\varphi_1\equiv0 \text{ on }(\mathbb{D}_{2r_1})^c,\text{ while } 
\varphi_2\equiv1 \text{ on }\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2\setminus\mathbb{D}_{r_1}
\text{ and }
\varphi_2\equiv0 \text{ on }\mathbb{D}_{r_1/2}
\end{equation*}
and with $|\nabla\varphi_i|^2+|\nabla^2\varphi_i|
\lesssim
r_1^{-2}$, we 
can hence get maps
$$
u_1=\pi_N\bigl(\varphi_1u+(1-\varphi_1)m\bigr) :\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2\to N \text{ and }
u_2:=\varphi_2u+(1-\varphi_2)m:\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2\to \ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^K\hookleftarrow N
$$
with $
u_1\equiv u$ on $\mathbb{D}_{r_1}$
and  $ u_1\equiv \pi_N(m)$ on $
\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2\setminus\mathbb{D}_{2r_1},
$ while 
$ u_2\equiv u$ on $ \ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2\setminus\mathbb{D}_{r_1} 
$ 
and $
u_2\equiv m$ on $ \mathbb{D}_{r_1/2},
$ for which 
\begin{equation*}\begin{aligned}
E(u_1)+E(u_2)-E(u)
&\lesssim
E(u,A)
+
r_1^{-2} \Vertu-\fint_A u\Vert_{L^2(A)}^2
\lesssim
\Vert\nabla u\Vert_{L^2(A)}^2
\lesssim
\mu^{-1/2}
\lesssim
\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^4.
\end{aligned}\end{equation*}
The claim hence follows once we show that 
both
\begin{equation}
\vertE(u_1)-E(\omega^*)\vert
\lesssim
\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^2
\label{claim:est1}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
E(u_2)
\lesssim
\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^2.
\label{claim:est2}
\end{equation}

\textbf{Proof of \eqref{claim:est1}.}\\
We first note that as $(r_1 \mu)^{-1}\sim \mu^{-1/2}$ we can bound
$$ 
\Vertu_1-\omega^*\circ\pi_{\mu}\Vert_{L^\infty(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)} \lesssim \text{osc}_A u + \Vertu-\omega^*\circ\pi_{\mu}\Vert_{L^\infty(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}+\text{osc}_{\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2\setminus \mathbb{D}_{r_1}}\pi_\mu\lesssim  \varepsilon+\mu^{-1/2} 
$$ and 
$$\Vert\nabla (u_1-\omega^*\circ\pi_{\mu})\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}
\lesssim E(u,A)^\frac{1}{2}+\Vert\nabla (u-\omega^*\circ\pi_{\mu})\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)} +\Vert\nabla \pi_\mu\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2\setminus \mathbb{D}_{r_1})}\lesssim \mu^{-1/4}+\varepsilon.
$$
A sufficiently small choice of $\varepsilon$ hence ensures that $\Vertu_1-\omega^*\circ\pi_{\mu}\Vert_{L^\infty(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}+\Vert\nabla (u_1-\omega^*\circ\pi_{\mu})\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}\leq \varepsilon_1$.
As these quantities remain invariant as we rescale $\mathbb{D}_{r_1}$ to $\mathbb{D}_1$ we hence deduce that $\tilde u_1:=u_1(r_1 x)$, which is by construction constant outside of $\mathbb{D}_2$, satisfies the assumptions of the proposition with $\tilde \mu:= r_1 \mu\sim \mu^{-1/2}$ in place of $\mu$ and $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_1$. This allows us to apply \eqref{est:Loj-with-logmu} for $\tilde u_1$ and $\tilde \mu$ to deduce that  
\begin{equation} \label{est:E-u1}
\vertE(u_1)-E(\omega^*)\vert=\vertE(u_1)-E(\omega^*)\vert
\lesssim
(\log\tilde \mu)^{\gamma/2}
\Vert\tau(\tilde u_1)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^\gamma.
\end{equation}
We now crucially use that the above rescaling significantly reduces the $L^2$ norm of the tension, namely that 
\begin{equation} 
\label{est:tension-tilde}
\Vert\tau(\tilde u_1)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}=r_1\Vert\tau(u_1)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}\leq r_1\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}+r_1 \Vert\tau(u_1)\Vert_{L^2(A)}.\end{equation} 
As the energy of $u$ is small on the larger annulus $A_2:=\mathbb{D}_{4r_1}\setminus\mathbb{D}_{r_1/4}$ standard $H^2$ estimates for almost harmonic maps as found e.g. in \cite[Lemma $2.1$]{dingtian} imply that 
\begin{equation*}
\int_{A} |\nabla^2u|^2+|\nabla u|^4
\lesssim
r_1^{-2}E(u,A_2)
+
\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(A_2)}^2.
\end{equation*}
Combined with the trivial pointwise bound $\vert\tau(u_1)\vert\lesssim \vert\nabla^2 u\vert+\vert\nabla u\vert^2+r_1^{-2} \vertu-m\vert+r_1^{-1}\vert\nabla u\vert \mathbbm{1}_A$ and the Poincar\'e inequality this allows us to deduce that 
$$\Vert\tau(u_1)\Vert_{L^2(A)}\lesssim r_1^{-1} E(u,A_2)^{1/2}+\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(A_2)}.$$
As $r_1\sim \mu^{-1/2}$ while $E(u,A_2)\lesssim \mu^{-1/2}$, compare \eqref{est:energy-A-larger}, we can hence bound  
$$r_1\Vert\tau(u_1)\Vert_{L^2(A)}\lesssim  E(u,A_2)^{1/2}+r_1\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(A_2)}\lesssim \mu^{-1/4}+\mu^{-1/2} \delta_1\lesssim \mu^{-1/4}.$$
Inserting this, \eqref{est:tension-tilde} and  $\log\tilde\mu\sim \log \mu$ into \eqref{est:E-u1} hence yields the desired bound of   
$$\vertE(u_1)-E(\omega^*)\vert
\lesssim
(\log \mu)^{\gamma/2} \mu^{-\gamma/4}\lesssim \mu^{-1/4}\lesssim \Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^2$$
since $\gamma>1$ and since $\mu$ satisfies \eqref{ass:case2}. 
\end{proof}

\paragraph{\textbf{Proof of \eqref{claim:est2}.}}
$ $\\
As $\nabla \varphi_2$ is supported on $A$ and  $u_2=u+(1-\varphi_2)(m-u)$, we have
pointwise bounds of 
\begin{equation*}\begin{aligned}
|\Delta u_2|
&\leq\varphi_2
|\Delta u|+2
|\nabla\varphi_2||\nabla u|+
|\Delta\varphi_2||u-m|
\\
&\lesssim
\varphi_2|\tau(u)|
+
\varphi_2|\nabla u|^2
+
\mathbbm{1}_A\bigl(r_1^{-1}|\nabla u|+r_1^{-2}|u-m|\bigr)\\
&\lesssim
|\tau(u)|
+
|\nabla u_2|^2
+
\mathbbm{1}_A\bigl(|\nabla u|^2+r_1^{-1}|\nabla u|+r_1^{-2}|u-m|\bigr).
\end{aligned}\end{equation*}
As $u$, and thus $u_2$, are constant outside of $\mathbb{D}_3$ we can combine the above estimate with the Poincar\'e inequality, applied on both $\mathbb{D}_3$ and on $A$, to estimate
\begin{equation*}\begin{aligned}
\int_{\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2}|\nabla u_2|^2&=\int_{\mathbb{D}_3}|\nabla u_2|^2
=
-\int_{\mathbb{D}_3}
\bigl(u_2-\fint_{\mathbb{D}_3}u_2\bigr)\cdot\Delta u_2
\\
&\lesssim
\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}
\Vert\nabla u_2\Vert_{L^2(\mathbb{D}_3)}
+\text{osc}(u_2) \int_{\mathbb{D}_3} \vert\nabla u_2\vert^2+E(u,A).
\end{aligned}\end{equation*}
As $\text{osc}(u_2)\lesssim
\text{osc}_{\mathbb{D}_{r_1}^c}(\omega^*\circ\pi_\mu)+\Vertu-\omega^*\circ\pi_{\mu}\Vert_{L^\infty}\lesssim (\mu r_1)^{-1}+\varepsilon\lesssim \mu^{-1/2}+\varepsilon$ is guaranteed to be small if $\varepsilon$ is small, we can  absorb the second term 
to deduce that
\begin{equation*}\begin{aligned}
\int_{\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2}|\nabla u_2|^2
&\lesssim
\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^2 
+
E(u,A)\lesssim \Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^2 +\mu^{-1/2} \lesssim\Vert\tau(u)\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}^2, 
\end{aligned}\end{equation*}
using \eqref{est:energy-A-larger} in the second and 
\eqref{ass:case2} in the last step. 

This establishes \eqref{claim:est2} and hence completes the proof of the proposition.

$ u_2\equiv u$ on $ \ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2\setminus\mathbb{D}_{r_1} 
$ 
and $

E(u,A)
+

We first note that as $(r_1 \mu)^{-1}\sim \mu^{-1/2}$ we can bound
$$ 
\Vertu_1-\omega^*\circ\pi_{\mu}\Vert_{L^\infty(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)} \lesssim \text{osc}_A u + \Vertu-\omega^*\circ\pi_{\mu}\Vert_{L^\infty(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)}+\text{osc}_{\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2\setminus \mathbb{D}_{r_1}}\pi_\mu\lesssim  \varepsilon+\mu^{-1/2} 
$$ and

\lesssim E(u,A)^\frac{1}{2}+\Vert\nabla (u-\omega^*\circ\pi_{\mu})\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2)} +\Vert\nabla \pi_\mu\Vert_{L^2(\ensuremath{{\mathbb R}}^2\setminus \mathbb{D}_{r_1})}\lesssim \mu^{-1/4}+\varepsilon.
$$

\begin{equation} \label{est:E-u1}
\vertE(u_1)-E(\omega^*)\vert=\vertE(u_1)-E(\omega^*)\vert
\lesssim

body_md: We can take $x = 0$ without loss of generality. The assumption (\ref{main:assumption}) implies (\ref{weightedloj:assumption}), with $\tau = \sqrt{T - t},$ for times $t$ sufficiently close to $T.$ By the previous theorem, for each such $t,$ the \L ojasiewicz inequality (\ref{weightedloj:loj}) is satisfied for $u = u(t).$ Since the quantity $\Phi_{\sqrt{T - t}}(u(t))$ is monotone-decreasing (see \cite{struwehmsurfaces} or \cite[Theorem 3.2]{waldronweighted}) and the set $\mathcal{E}_0$ is finite, by further advancing $t,$ we can assume that (\ref{weightedloj:loj}) is satisfied for the same value $E_1 \in \mathcal{E}_0$ at all times. The hypothesis of \cite[Corollary 4.3]{waldronweighted} is therefore satisfied, giving the desired conclusions.
